name: Mexico City
tagline: Ancient worlds, modern art and a city worth eating through
summary: Build separate days around the historic centre, Chapultepec and Coyoacán. Teotihuacán is a dedicated excursion; Xochimilco requires its own south-city time allowance.
seasonNote: High-altitude city with mild days and cool evenings. Summer brings frequent afternoon rain; heat and air quality vary.
arrival: Use the airport printed on your ticket: Benito Juárez (MEX) and Felipe Ángeles (NLU) have very different transfers. Use authorised airport transport and allow city traffic time.
gettingAround: Group stops by district. Metro, Metrobús and taxis can be useful; road journeys across the city are slower than map distances suggest.
cashTip: Carry small peso notes for markets and casual food; use cards at established businesses and keep a daily-cash limit.
foodTip: Choose the actual restaurant branch and dish. Al pastor usually means pork; vegetarian and halal filters must rely on named-venue evidence.
buyTip: La Ciudadela offers crafts from across Mexico; compare workmanship, materials and transport-friendly sizes.
baseArea: Roma/Condesa for cafés and neighbourhood walks, or Reforma/Centro for central sights; put the exact hotel into the proximity planner.

items.name: National Museum of Anthropology
items.summary: Build a visual foundation for Mexico’s ancient cultures before visiting archaeological sites.
items.expect: A large indoor museum with enough material for far more than a short stop.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Major archaeological collections make the museum a strong orientation stop for first-time visitors.
The central courtyard and umbrella-like canopy add a memorable architectural setting.
visitFlow: Choose two or three culture galleries instead of trying every room.
Use the Mexica gallery as context before Teotihuacán or the historic centre.
items.tradeoffs: Museum fatigue is real; older official pages show outdated prices, so use the current Culture listing.

items.name: Chapultepec Castle · National History Museum
items.summary: Walk up to a hilltop castle with historical rooms and city views.
items.expect: A hill approach followed by a museum; water and bag rules require planning.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The palace rooms give Mexican national history a domestic and political setting.
Terraces look out across Chapultepec and Reforma.
visitFlow: Allow time for the uphill approach.
Visit the historical rooms and finish at the permitted terraces.
items.tradeoffs: Closed Mondays; a large afternoon can be tiring after the Anthropology Museum.

items.name: Zócalo & Metropolitan Cathedral
items.summary: Orient yourself in the immense civic square and surrounding historic buildings.
items.expect: A living civic space affected by events, demonstrations and religious services.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Rating applies to Zócalo square, not a combined count including the cathedral. Review count is not visitor footfall.

whyVisit: The plaza brings the city’s civic, religious and pre-Hispanic layers together in one area.
Cathedral architecture provides a distinct interior experience when access is open.
visitFlow: Walk the square and identify the cathedral and nearby Templo Mayor area.
Enter the cathedral respectfully if services and access allow.
items.tradeoffs: Some nearby museums and palace visits have separate entry arrangements.

items.name: Frida Kahlo Museum · Casa Azul
items.summary: Visit the artist’s blue house, garden and personal environment.
items.expect: A compact, popular house museum with a fixed entry window.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Domestic rooms and belongings make the biography tangible.
The garden and blue-walled house give a clear sense of place beyond reproductions of paintings.
visitFlow: Book the official timed ticket before arranging the day.
Follow the house route, then leave time for the garden and Coyoacán streets.
items.tradeoffs: No ordinary ticket-window sales listed; advance booking and punctual arrival matter.

items.name: Teotihuacán archaeological zone
items.summary: Explore the monumental avenues and pyramids of a major ancient city.
items.expect: A long, exposed archaeological walk plus separate road transfer.
items.tip: Do not assume pyramid climbing is allowed; the 2026 official guidance prohibits ascending the Pyramid of the Sun.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The scale of the pyramids and urban plan is best understood on foot.
On-site museums add objects and context to the monumental landscape.
visitFlow: Arrive early with water and sun protection.
Walk the permitted avenue-and-plaza route and add a site museum if open.
items.tradeoffs: Heat, long walking distances and cross-city transfers require a dedicated day.

items.name: Xochimilco canals · trajinera ride
items.summary: Take a colourful flat-bottomed boat through the historic canal landscape.
items.expect: Some routes are lively with music and vendors; a quiet ecological route needs deliberate planning.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Official municipal rate retrieved: MXN 750 per trajinera per hour, maximum 18 people. Range is 1–2 hours for the whole boat. Divide only among your actual group; transport, food and extras separate.

review.note: No verified numeric snapshot for this exact listing; open current reviews. This is an editorial recommendation, not measured footfall.

whyVisit: The canals connect the present city with the older chinampa agricultural system.
A private group boat creates a shared outing with a pace different from museums.
visitFlow: Choose an official embarcadero and agree the route and total boat price before departure.
Take the canal circuit and pay extras only if you choose them.
items.tradeoffs: The quoted official rate is per boat per hour, not per person; road transfers add time.

whyVisit: The marble exterior gives the historic centre one of its most recognisable buildings.

items.summary: Browse crafts, textiles, ceramics and metalwork from across Mexico.
items.expect: Free browsing; the price range is an optional souvenir allowance.
items.tip: Check the official page before setting out.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: No verified numeric snapshot for this exact listing; open current reviews. This is an editorial recommendation, not measured footfall.

whyVisit: The market gathers regional craft traditions in one accessible location.
Small textiles and artisan objects can be easier to carry than larger souvenir pieces.
visitFlow: Compare materials and workmanship across a few stalls.
Ask where a piece was made and plan safe packing before purchasing.
items.tradeoffs: Quality and provenance vary by stall; the craft market is distinct from the nearby library.

items.name: Pujol
items.summary: Enrique Olvera’s influential two-star restaurant, which helped define modern Mexican cuisine. Its aged mole is famous.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
items.priceNote: Per-person planning estimate from the MICHELIN price band ($$$$), not a menu quote; drinks, service and tax may add to the total.
items.bestTime: Lunch or dinner by reservation; check the current service days

whyVisit: Enrique Olvera’s influential two-star restaurant, which helped define modern Mexican cuisine. Its aged mole is famous.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Two MICHELIN Stars (excellent cooking), a rare level of recognition.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.

dietary.note: No dietary evidence collected yet. Ask the restaurant directly about halal, vegetarian and allergy needs; tasting menus need notice.
